outcome_intro: Ask your AI "which client VMs don't have a good, recent, verified backup right now?" and get one row per guest across every client's Proxmox cluster: is it in an enabled job, how old is its newest real restore point, did Proxmox Backup Server verify it. Every request this skill sends to Proxmox is a read; it never starts, stops, restores or deletes anything.

instead_of_say.instead: Logging into each client's Proxmox VE and Backup Server web UI every morning to read task lists and backup emails
instead_of_say.say: Which client VMs don't have a good, recent, verified backup right now?

instead_of_say.instead: Finding out a new VM was never added to an enabled backup job on the day the client asks for a restore
instead_of_say.say: Which VMs or disks are not in any enabled backup job, and why?

instead_of_say.instead: Opening PBS verify task logs one by one to see how far a verify failure spread
instead_of_say.say: Which backup groups failed verification, and do they still have a good restore point?

pain_points: A Proxmox shop with many clients runs one cluster and often one Backup Server per client, so "are all my clients' backups good?" means a login per site and a scroll through task lists.

A green backup task does not mean every guest was backed up. A multi-guest vzdump job only names the guest that failed inside its task log, and a VM created after a job with a fixed VM list was set up is in no job at all.
Verify failures spread quietly. On a central PBS that more than 100 servers back up to, the weekly verify job showed a growing count of failed snapshots before anyone traced the cause.
Most MSPs will not hand an AI agent a token that can stop, change or delete a VM, so an agent that has to manage the hypervisor never gets connected at all.

outcomes.question: Which client VMs don't have a good, recent, verified backup?
Which VMs or disks are in no enabled backup job?
What failed or stopped part-way overnight, by guest, with the error line?
How far has a PBS verify failure spread?
Which backup datastores fill up within 30 days?
Can we restore VM 104, and from which verified points?
Did every scheduled backup produce a restore point this month, per client?

different_vs_wrappers: Most Proxmox MCP servers are built to operate one cluster: list VMs, start and stop them, take snapshots, with the dangerous actions behind a flag. This one sends Proxmox nothing but reads, and its compound commands join each guest's job coverage, the real archives on every backup storage, PBS verify state and the vzdump task logs, across every client cluster, into one verdict per guest.
different_vs_vendor: Proxmox has no built-in AI assistant. The Proxmox VE and Backup Server web interfaces show jobs, tasks and datastores; this adds a per-guest backup verdict joined across both products and across every client, and it changes nothing in either.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, and proxmox-mcp speaks HTTP natively: set PROXMOX_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN to a long random value, run `proxmox-mcp --transport http` (it serves `http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp` and refuses to start without that token), and put that /mcp endpoint behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.
Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Can the AI stop, change or delete anything on my Proxmox hosts?
faqs.a: No. The CLI and MCP server only contain read (GET) calls to Proxmox VE and Proxmox Backup Server; there is no command that starts, stops, migrates, restores, prunes or deletes anything. The only writes are local files: the cluster list, a saved token, the local mirror (which the per-endpoint read commands also update), the agent learning store, and a response cache of raw API answers (owner-only files; the backup commands never answer from it). One side effect to know: reading a storage's status lets Proxmox mount an enabled storage, which its own status daemon already does every 10 seconds.

faqs.q: What API token does it need?
faqs.a: A privilege-separated API token for each product. Proxmox Backup Server: the Audit role on / (read-only). Proxmox VE: PVEAuditor on /. One catch: Proxmox VE lists backup files only to a token that also holds Datastore.AllocateSpace and VM.Backup, so if your backups live on dir, NFS or CIFS storage, or you have not configured the Backup Server here, add a custom role with those two privileges. An audit-only token is reported as "storage not read" and the guest as unproven, never as "no backups". If your backups are on Proxmox Backup Server and PROXMOX_PBS_HOST is set (spelled as in the PVE storage's server field: the same IP or hostname), the CLI reads them from the PBS API and the PVE token can stay audit-only. On a stock install the local storage also accepts backups: with an audit-only token it is listed under fetch failures (its guests keep their verdicts), and posture --fail-on-red exits 1 until you remove "VZDump backup file" from its content types or grant it the two privileges. Grant the roles on / (propagating) and put no NoAccess or narrower ACL below it: Proxmox leaves out of every list the guests and storages a token cannot see, and while the CLI flags a missing or narrowed grant, an explicit NoAccess on one guest is invisible to any read. The PVE token is USER@REALM!TOKENID=SECRET; the PBS token uses a colon before the secret.

faqs.q: Proxmox uses a self-signed certificate. Do I have to turn off certificate checks?
faqs.a: No, and there is no option to. Pin the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (shown under the node's Certificates) with PROXMOX_TLS_FINGERPRINT and PROXMOX_PBS_TLS_FINGERPRINT, or per client cluster in clusters.toml. A PVE pin never vouches for the PBS host.

faqs.q: How do I cover many client clusters?
faqs.a: Add one entry per client with `proxmox-cli clusters add`: its PVE host, optional PBS host and namespace, certificate fingerprints, and the names of the environment variables that hold its tokens (never the tokens themselves). The fleet commands then run across every configured cluster; `--cluster` or `--client` narrows to one. For an MCP client, add those token variables to the MCP server's env block too. On a shared Backup Server, give each client cluster its own PBS namespace (or datastore): VMIDs repeat across clusters, so where two clusters write the same namespace the CLI cannot tell whose vm/100 a snapshot is, reports the overlap, and does not count those restore points.

governance_summary: Every request this skill sends to Proxmox VE or Proxmox Backup Server is a read, so no command it runs can change a cluster or a backup. The only writes are local: the cluster list, a saved token, the local mirror and the agent learning store, and the MCP server cannot edit the cluster list. Gate where output goes: --deliver can send any command's output to a file or a webhook URL.
